unit: A diagnostic difference d is score(arm) - score(reference), so a positive mean d is a loss for the arm; every table says which way it points. Scores are grid CRPS, upper-tail twCRPS and the Brier score of P(> +5 bp) (docs/decisions/pressure-probability.md), as in #1321. Percentages are skill, 1 - mean(arm)/mean(reference).
intervals: the 90% interval of the stationary block bootstrap (mean block 10, 2000 replications, seed 1344, resampling in date order) over the units of the group, repo_model.metrics.stationary_bootstrap_intervals. It is a diagnostic interval on mean d, not scoring protocol v1's studentized test (the studentized figures are #1321's and are quoted from its record); no row is a verdict; a group of fewer than 20 units is listed and given no interval. A reading is taken from the interval excluding zero; otherwise undecided. The intervals of a group of target days keep the current method (the group's days resampled in date order as if consecutive), which #1221 questions.

H-f.claim: The Brier gain of (s3c-ann-flagnet) against (s3c-ann-net) sits on settlement-day targets and on the cells where the spread exceeded +5 bp: adding the flag back restores the settlement shift the net shrank (#1320), which matters when the spread is high.
H-f.reading: supported when on the settlement-day target cells the interval of mean d (Brier) lies below zero and on the neither-settles cells it does not lie below zero, and the Brier difference summed over the event cells is a gain on its interval; not supported when the neither-settles cells show a gain on their interval and the settlement-day cells do not; otherwise undecided.

H-g.claim: The 2020 loss of (s3c-ann-flagnet) against (s3c-ann-net) is an over-shift: the flagnet's fitted settlement shift on 2020 settlement-day targets exceeds the realised settlement-day premium, so its forecast is too high on those days.
H-g.reading: supported when, at leads 2 to 5, the 2020 fitted shift's interval lies above the upper end of the premium's interval and the settlement-day bias (error on settlement-day targets less that on the others) of (s3c-ann-flagnet) has an interval below zero, and the 2020 loss on grid CRPS on the settlement-day target cells is a loss on its interval; not supported when the shift's interval does not lie above the premium's or the bias interval contains zero; otherwise undecided.

H-h.claim: The 2020 loss sits on the immediate-release cash management bill days (the announcement of such a bill states no release time, so its 12:00 dating is unverified, Lens E item G).
H-h.reading: supported when the 2020 loss on grid CRPS is a loss on its interval with those days in and is not a loss (undecided or a gain) with them left out; not supported when it stays a loss on its interval with them left out; not read when the 2020 difference is not a loss on its interval with them in; otherwise undecided. The same rule is applied with (s3c-ann) as the reference, to say whether the loss belongs to the net term.

power.what: The power of the prospective comparison drafted in metadata/s3c_flagnet_prospective_draft_1344.json, read off the development window's daily difference d = score((s3c-ann-net)) - score((s3c-ann-flagnet)) (positive favours the arm) on grid CRPS averaged over h = 1..5 (primary) and upper-tail twCRPS (key secondary), one number per decision day.
power.series: the decision days from 2020-04-03 (where every confirmation day falls: scoring-protocol.md, draft amendment 2, #886) to the last development day, so the heavy-tailed pre-2020 days do not set the variance
power.method: repo_model.scoring_protocol: the critical value of each look is calibrate_critical_value on the centred series at nominal_levels() (looks 125 and 250; look 60 checks futility only) with windows of the look's length drawn by window_t_statistics (circular blocks of 10, 20,000 windows, seed 1344); power at a true effect delta is the share of windows of the series centred and shifted by delta whose studentized mean (Newey-West lag 10) exceeds the look's value. Looks are not combined (the share that crosses at each look on its own), a lower bound on the share that crosses at either. The effects are the arm's observed development mean d, and a skill of 0.5%, 1% and 3% of the mean score of (s3c-ann-net). A true effect of zero is run as a size check. The days-needed figure is the analytic ((z(alpha) + z(0.8)) * sigma_LR / delta) squared, with sigma_LR the Newey-West long-run standard deviation of the series
power.multiplicity: the same run is repeated with alpha divided by the size of the family (1, 2 and 3), the cost of Holm's first step when the arm is one of the secondaries and the key secondary metric is tested beside (scoring-protocol.md section 8)
power.reading: descriptive: development data, an estimate of what the prospective comparison can show, not a threshold. No minimum power is set here; that is hers

reading_rules: A figure is a check on days that were already seen. Nothing here is a verdict, nothing is registered and no choice is made on it; (s3c-ann-net) stays the candidate of avenue #1318 and (s3c) the H5 candidate until she rules.
A gain or loss is read from the 90% interval of mean d excluding zero; otherwise undecided. A point estimate alone is not read.
A pooled figure is never read without the regime, lead and settlement-day-type splits beside it.
The bill leg and the net bill are read with Lens E's caveat on the announcement time of a cash management bill.
Whether to register the arm beside the candidate goes to her as a marked question with numbered options and a default that changes no claim.
